Term,Definition
blowdown rate,This rate of pressure relief is set to allow a controlled expansion of any gas trapped inside the cable and to give it time to start to migrate out of the cable. The recommended blowdown rate is 50 psi/min.

columns: The pressure drop allowed on each blowdown stage. Fifty percent maximum step blowdown is recommended to prevent any trapped gas from expanding to a volume large enough to damage the cable before it is allowed to migrate out of the cable.

rows.The pressure drop allowed on each blowdo: The time between each step blowdown. Once any trapped gas has expanded to its maximum volume during the 50% maximum step blowdown it is essential that time is given for this expanded gas to migrate out of the cable before proceeding to the next blowdown stage. The recommended rest period is 30 minutes.

The final pressure after the last blowdown stage. Although the potential expansion is at its greatest, once below this threshold, the mechanical integrity of the cable is sufficient to contain the pressure until it dissipates normally. The recommended final threshold is 500 psi or less.

This can be atmospheric in most cases but there may be variances. For example, a minimum positive pressure is maintained in an installation where the thermal dynamics may induce an undesirable vacuum in the annulus when the well is shut in.
